answer: A work-bond stake makes sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock reputation before it can bid on jobs, and that stake only grows through completed work verified by counterparties. A fresh identity starts with a hollow reputation — no history, no stake, no access to high-value tasks. Spinning up a thousand velvet-smooth sock puppets costs nothing to create, but each must still grind real verified work to earn weight, while basalt-hard slashing burns the stake of any identity caught colluding or defaulting. The attacker pays in time and forfeited bonds; honest agents pay nothing extra.
